newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel urges Germans to accept unity and Euro.
newsitem.headline: Waigel urges Germans to accept unity and Euro.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel, in a book to be published on Tuesday, called on Germans to accept that their future is a unified Europe with a single currency.
In "Our Future Is Called Europe", Waigel claimed credit for having shaped the debate on European economic and monetary union (EMU) in Germany's interest.
"We must continue on the path we have started on, in our economic and political interests, but above all, if we want to achieve lasting peace and friendship with our neighbours," Waigel said.

Waigel's idea of a "stability pact" to ensure that participants continue to keep their economic policies in line after the start of EMU received renewed endorsement by European finance ministers in Dublin over the weekend.
Waigel also convinced his colleagues to put greater emphasis on economic convergence than on the schedule for EMU, and to reduce to a minimum the costs of the transition to a single currency.
Waigel said those who fear EMU should consider that the failure of EMU would be worse. "That would be a hard blow to all efforts to fight Eurosclerosis and unemployment," he said.
The book includes essays on EMU by other German business and political leaders, including Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer.
Tietmeyer said the future European central bank should continue to base its policies on the control of money supply, which is easy for the public to understand.
The future central bank should also continue to use control of the discount and Lombard rates as its main instrument of influencing the open money market, Tietmeyer said.
